title: Bounded multivariate polynomial Wasm core
objective: Profile public multivariate GCD/resultant/Groebner workloads and deliver the highest-impact bounded FLINT shared core with exact packed ABI, native/direct-Wasm/public proof evidence, fallback contract, tracing handoff, and benchmark bounds

oracles: Existing public Sage.js native FLINT multivariate API
Sage-compatible ordinary polynomial identities and normalization

handoff.summary: Profiled representative supported public 3-variable GCD, resultant, and Groebner workloads and selected exact ZZ resultant as the highest-impact viable route (39.23 ms versus 0.81 ms and 0.18 ms). Added a host-neutral bounded FLINT fmpz_mpoly_resultant packed core with canonical GMP limb transport, deterministic cleanup, explicit status codes, one coarse mathematical crossing, malformed/unsupported/resource separation, a native C differential, a real wasm32-wasip1 execution proof, public Node native/disabled parity, and a checked benchmark/bounds record. The representative packed core takes 4,928 input bytes, returns 32,192 output bytes, and ran in 36.12 ms warm median.
risks: Public polynomial dispatch, the lazy FLINT Wasm artifact adapter, browser-side sparse ZZ materialization, fixed private route recording, build/native-code registries, and the public real-browser proof are intentionally integration-owned and are not changed by this narrow lane; production browser resultant does not use the core until that handoff lands.

The FLINT call is not cooperatively cancellable once entered. The core therefore fails closed at 256 terms per operand, 512 coefficient bits, elimination degree 8, parameter total degree 8 per term, derived resultant parameter degree 128, 1 MiB ingress, and 16 MiB egress; the browser adapter should retain its worker reset policy.

Windows uses the existing exact native-addon fallback. The standalone core/direct-Wasm proof ran on Linux x64; integration CI must compile and execute the selected artifact on Linux arm64, macOS arm64, and Windows x64 fallback paths.
The 100 ms native and 250 ms browser budgets are initial bounded targets. Native Linux is measured, but Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit measurements must be captured after public integration.

pnpm test:changed completed the repository build but stopped at a pre-existing integration-base package-graph error because src/lib/sagejs/kernels/matrix/combinatorial.py has no package owner. All four task-required validation commands pass, including the full pnpm test:native suite.
next_steps: Compile multivariate_wasm_core.c into the lazy exact FLINT wasm32-wasip1 artifact and expose the single packed function through the bounded Wasm adapter with a 16 MiB initial output reservation.
Add only the browser-side sparse ZZ host representation needed to marshal and materialize the public result; keep the actual resultant computation entirely inside FLINT.

Wire MultivariatePolynomialElement.resultant so supported ZZ inputs select this route while preserving parent, ordering, eliminated-variable, result-normalization, and exact native fallback semantics; unsupported browser inputs must raise the documented capability error.

Record the private route identifier wasm-library:flint:fmpz-mpoly-resultant-packed-v1 with target wasm32-wasip1, one mathematical call, ingress/egress bytes, crossing count one, and total copied bytes without exporting the tracing constructor.

Extend Node-Wasm and real-browser public tests with the exact representative source, requiring equality with native, the fixed route, 4,928/32,192-byte accounting, one crossing, no portable computation, and forced-off native fallback/browser capability behavior.

Classify the new C file as an external-library adapter in architecture/native-code.json, add it to the shared native/Wasm boundary inventory and build registries, then run architecture:check, test:changed, and cross-platform browser receipts at the integrated commit.
